request.subject: Both Engines Died Over New York City - part 1: Geese Knocked Out Both Engines Over New York
request.title: Both Engines Died Over New York City (Part 1/3)
request.description:
A flock of geese, two dead engines, and a jet gliding over New York City with minutes to spare. Where would you have tried to land?

Part 1 of 3: Both Engines Died Over New York City

Sources:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Airways_Flight_1549
https://www.ntsb.gov/investigations/AccidentReports/Reports/AAR1003.pdf
https://flightsafety.org/asw-article/survival-on-the-hudson/

Stock footage: Pexels. Made with AI-assisted narration.

#shorts #truestory

extra_params.video_script: A packed jet lost both engines just minutes after takeoff. And its captain would pick the strangest runway in New York. It was a freezing January afternoon, and the plane had just left LaGuardia Airport. Then it flew straight into a flock of Canada geese. Birds were sucked into both engines, and the power died. Now the jet was gliding, low over one of the biggest cities on Earth. The pilots had only minutes to find somewhere to land. Captain Sully Sullenberger chose the frigid Hudson River. Subscribe so you don't miss Part 2.
